newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hog market mixed - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hog market mixed - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices were mixed early Tuesday, dealers said. Prices in the eastern Corn Belt were underpinned by "decent" meat packer demand and light marketings, they said.
However, prices in the western belt were showing signs of weakness following rain Monday, which forced a delay in corn harvesting and allowed farmers more time to sell hogs.

Iowa and southern Minnesota hog prices were steady to $0.50 lower, with $51.50 to $52.00 in the country and $52.50 to $54.00 at plants. Some packer buyers said they already had half of Wednesday's slaughter inventory booked.
Illinois hog prices were steady amid light hog marketings, with $52.50 to $53.00/country and $53.00 to $53.50/ plants.

Indiana hog prices were steady to up $0.50, with $52.00 to $52.50 in the country and $53.00 to $53.50 at plants. Ohio hog prices were steady, with $50.00 in the country and $51.00 to $52.00 at plants.

Light support was generated by moderate pork demand and thin advances Monday in pork cut-out values, with losses in hams and trimmings offset by gains in loins and butts, market sources said. There were 65.4 pork loads and 17.0 loads of trimmings sold, according to USDA.
